summary: Edge cookie corruption causes hidden cohort divergence during canary rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Hermes AI reported stochastic model-version divergence for a subset (~12%) of API keys during a canary rollout. Customers who were previously pinned to rw-instruct-1.3 started seeing responses from opt-6.7b intermittently. This happened only during the canary window and affected a coherent cohort of tenants behind the same edge POP.

Impact:
- Enterprise customer Hermes AI observed inconsistent inference outputs for production traffic (non-deterministic model variants).
- Customer reported functional regressions in a QA test suite (generation style/quality mismatch).
- Business impact: reduced confidence in rollout, paused further canary progression.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod (us-east-1)
- Canary: rw-instruct-1.3 (new) weighted 15% vs baseline rw-instruct-1.2
- Affected keys routed through edge-pop: pop-nyc-2 (edge-proxy version 3.4.1)
- Serving runtime versions: 1.9.4 (baseline) / 2.0.0-canary

Steps to reproduce (customer and support):
1) Hermes sends steady traffic using API key X-REDACTED through pop-nyc-2.
2) Customer pins sessions to rw-instruct-1.2 in their local session metadata.
3) During canary window, some requests still return opt-6.7b responses (different model family).

Observed behavior:
- ~12% of requests from the affected cohort returned tokens generated by opt-6.7b.
- Edge logs show a header rewrite on a subset of connections (X-RD-ROUTE) where model variant metadata was overwritten with an older persona that maps to a different routing bucket.

Expected behavior:
- Requests from pinned sessions should be consistently routed to the pinned model version; canary traffic may be routed to canary variant only when allowed by rollout policy. No cross-model family responses expected.

Key logs / traces (excerpt):
- edge-pop-nyc-2/access.log: "2026-03-10T14:32:05Z api_key=X-REDACTED route=rw-instruct-1.2 -> proxy:rewrite X-RD-ROUTE=rw-instruct-1.3"
- edge-pop-nyc-2/proxy-debug: "hdr-sanitize: trimmed cookie 'rw_session' length->0 for connection id 0x7f2a"
- reconciler-audit: "2026-03-10T14:32:07Z reconcile: canary-weight 15% assigned cohort hash bucket 0x1f3a -> rw-instruct-1.3"
- serving-runtime: trace shows fallback to opt-6.7b for requests where KV cache miss + fallback policy triggered during cache warm-up.

Additional notes:
- The customer uses session pins in custom headers instead of standard session cookie for historical reasons.
- Affected cohort correlates with edge connections that had TLS renegotiations within 60s of the request.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge header sanitizer in proxy 3.4.1 trims non-standard session headers during TLS renegotiation, causing loss of pin metadata leading to default/fallback routing.
Hypothesis 2: Reconciler cohort namespace contains stale routing tags that map hash buckets to legacy model families (opt-6.7b), introduced by a previous migration in 2025 that missed key clears.
Reproduction: Local TLS renegotiation + edge-proxy 3.4.1 reliably reproduces header trim for custom headers matching pattern 'rw_*' when connection reused and renegotiated within 60s.

Correlation: All affected requests observed via pop-nyc-2 and client connections showing TLS renegotiation in edge logs. Strong statistical correlation (p<0.001) between renegotiation events and divergence.
Interim mitigation validated: Edge patch disabling aggressive trim removes the majority of divergence, confirming header trimming is necessary precondition.
Reconciler fix required: Clear legacy bucket tags and harden cohort mapping to prefer explicit pin metadata; add validation at reconcile time to prevent legacy tag reappearance.
Follow-up: Add canary safety check to detect cross-family response variance (e.g., mismatched model family) and auto-halt canary if variance > 1% for any customer cohort.
Related runbook: canary-rollout (link in related_confluence_pages) needs a section for header-mutation and edge-POP TLS interactions.
resolution: Workaround applied: patched edge-pop-nyc-2 to stop trimming rw_session-like headers during TLS renegotiation; forced tenant override for Hermes to maintain pin consistency. Engineering prepared reconciler migration PR to purge legacy bucket tags (PR submitted). Permanent rollout plan: reconciler PR merged and staged to prod (target 2026-03-15), followed by a controlled canary resumption. Runbook updated and alerting added to detect cross-family variance. Customer informed and monitoring in place.
